section: S&T institutions - CSIR and its laboratories, DST, DBT, DSIR, SERB
subsections: DST - establishment, mandate, autonomous institutes, flagship schemes
DSIR - PSUs (CEL, NRDC), in-house R&D recognition

accepted.s: The Department of Science and Technology (DST) was established in which year?
accepted.x: The Department of Science and Technology was established in 1971.
accepted.tq: Use the year-based numerical recall method and distinguish establishment dates from legislative dates.
accepted.sec: DST - establishment, mandate, autonomous institutes, flagship schemes

accepted.s: Which one of the following most appropriately describes the mandate of the Department of Science and Technology?
o: Regulation of all pharmaceutical manufacturing units
Administration of all higher educational institutions in India
Development of new areas of science and technology, R&D infrastructure, national missions and science policy
Coordination of defence procurement and military production
accepted.x: DST is the nodal department for new science and technology areas, R&D infrastructure, national missions and science policy.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution by its core mandate rather than by a neighbouring ministry’s function.
accepted.sec: DST - establishment, mandate, autonomous institutes, flagship schemes

accepted.s:
Consider the following institutions:
1. Bose Institute
2. JNCASR
3. Raman Research Institute
4. Wadia Institute
Which of the above are autonomous bodies associated with the Department of Science and Technology?
accepted.x: Bose Institute, JNCASR, Raman Research Institute and Wadia Institute are among the autonomous bodies associated with DST.
accepted.tq: Use an all-inclusive statement set when every listed institution belongs to the same institutional group.
accepted.sec: DST - establishment, mandate, autonomous institutes, flagship schemes

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT an autonomous body listed under the Department of Science and Technology?
accepted.x: NRDC is a public sector undertaking controlled by DSIR, not an autonomous body listed under DST. ARIES, Wadia Institute and BSIP are associated with DST.
accepted.tq: Find the institutional mismatch by separating DST autonomous bodies from DSIR public sector undertakings.
accepted.sec: DST - establishment, mandate, autonomous institutes, flagship schemes

accepted.s: Survey of India, including the National Institute for Geo-informatics Science and Technology (NIGST), Hyderabad, is placed under which department?
o: Department of Scientific and Industrial Research
accepted.x: Survey of India, including NIGST at Hyderabad, is under the Department of Science and Technology.
accepted.tq: Use the ‘who controls this institution?’ method to avoid swapping neighbouring science departments.
accepted.sec: DST - establishment, mandate, autonomous institutes, flagship schemes

accepted.s: Which of the following schemes is specifically associated with encouraging scientific interest and talent among students?
accepted.x: INSPIRE is a flagship scheme of DST associated with promoting scientific interest and talent.
accepted.tq: Match the scheme with its broad purpose before considering the department administering it.
accepted.sec: DST - establishment, mandate, autonomous institutes, flagship schemes

accepted.s: Vigyan Jyoti and STI Hubs for SC/ST are schemes associated with which institution?
o: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research only
Department of Scientific and Industrial Research
accepted.x: Vigyan Jyoti and STI Hubs for SC/ST are DST schemes.
accepted.tq: Group related schemes under their parent department instead of treating each scheme as a separate institution.
accepted.sec: DST - establishment, mandate, autonomous institutes, flagship schemes

accepted.s: The National Mission on Interdisciplinary Cyber-Physical Systems (NM-ICPS) was launched in which year with an outlay of ₹3,660 crore?
accepted.x: NM-ICPS was launched in 2018 with an outlay of ₹3,660 crore.
accepted.tq: Check both the year and the financial figure together; the two-part numerical combination is the key discriminator.
accepted.sec: DST - establishment, mandate, autonomous institutes, flagship schemes

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a scheme or initiative associated with the Department of Science and Technology in the material listed?
accepted.x: Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship is a return fellowship in the SERB and ANRF context. Nano Mission, Vigyan Jyoti and INSPIRE are associated with DST.
accepted.tq: Separate departmental flagship schemes from fellowships administered in the research-grant system.
accepted.sec: DST - establishment, mandate, autonomous institutes, flagship schemes

accepted.s:
The Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Scheme has DST as its nodal department. Which of the following are associated with this scheme?
1. LENSD
2. VIS
3. CDX
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: DST is nodal for the RDI Scheme, and LENSD, VIS and CDX are associated with it.
accepted.tq: When all listed components belong to one scheme, test the complete combination rather than a single abbreviation.
accepted.sec: DST - establishment, mandate, autonomous institutes, flagship schemes

accepted.s: FAIR is funded in what proportion by the Department of Science and Technology and the Department of Atomic Energy?
accepted.x: FAIR is funded equally by DST and DAE, in a 50:50 proportion.
accepted.tq: Use the proportion directly and distinguish equal co-funding from unequal partnership ratios.
accepted.sec: DST - establishment, mandate, autonomous institutes, flagship schemes

accepted.s: The Department of Scientific and Industrial Research (DSIR) was established in:
accepted.x: DSIR was established in January 1985.
accepted.tq: Retain the month-year combination when the question concerns departmental establishment.
accepted.sec: DSIR - PSUs (CEL, NRDC), in-house R&D recognition

accepted.s: DSIR is one of how many departments of the Ministry of Science and Technology?
accepted.x: DSIR is one of the three departments of the Ministry of Science and Technology.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the number of departments in a ministry from the number of organisations controlled by one department.
accepted.sec: DSIR - PSUs (CEL, NRDC), in-house R&D recognition

accepted.s:
Which of the following public sector undertakings are controlled by DSIR?
1. National Research Development Corporation (NRDC)
2. Central Electronics Limited (CEL)
3. Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: DSIR controls two public sector undertakings, NRDC and CEL. CSIR is controlled by DSIR but is not a public sector undertaking; it is a research organisation.
accepted.tq: Separate the department’s controlled research body from the two entities specifically classified as PSUs.
accepted.sec: DSIR - PSUs (CEL, NRDC), in-house R&D recognition

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes DSIR’s recognition of in-house research and development facilities?
o: It recognises only government laboratories and excludes private industry.
It recognises fewer than 500 in-house R&D centres and no SIROs.
It recognises more than 2,000 in-house R&D centres, more than 900 SIROs and more than 500 public-funded institutions.
It recognises only universities for customs-duty concessions.
accepted.x: DSIR recognises more than 2,000 in-house R&D centres, more than 900 SIROs and more than 500 public-funded institutions.
accepted.tq: Compare the scale figures as a group and reject options that reverse the ‘more than’ ranges.
accepted.sec: DSIR - PSUs (CEL, NRDC), in-house R&D recognition

accepted.s: Recognition by DSIR makes eligible in-house R&D centres and other recognised institutions for which of the following benefits?
o: Income tax and customs duty exemptions
accepted.x: DSIR recognition makes the recognised institutions eligible for income tax and customs duty exemptions.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional recognition to its stated fiscal consequence rather than to unrelated regulatory benefits.
accepted.sec: DSIR - PSUs (CEL, NRDC), in-house R&D recognition

accepted.s:
Which of the following are components of the Umbrella Industrial R&D scheme of DSIR?
1. PRISM
2. PACE
3. BIRD-crf
4. A2K+
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: PRISM, PACE, BIRD-crf and A2K+ are all components of DSIR’s Umbrella Industrial R&D scheme.
accepted.tq: Use the complete-list option when all four named sub-schemes are components of the same umbrella scheme.
accepted.sec: DSIR - PSUs (CEL, NRDC), in-house R&D recognition

accepted.s: The Core Research Grant and SERB-POWER are associated with which organisation?
accepted.x: Core Research Grant and SERB-POWER are grants associated with the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB).
accepted.tq: Identify the organisation from the distinctive prefix and purpose of its grant schemes.
accepted.sec: SERB - grants and status after ANRF

accepted.s: SERB-POWER primarily supports which category of researchers?
o: Scientists working exclusively in public sector undertakings
Only researchers below 25 years of age
Only overseas scientists of Indian origin
accepted.x: SERB-POWER is a grant initiative for women researchers.
accepted.tq: Use the beneficiary group as the direct discriminator between similarly named fellowship schemes.
accepted.sec: SERB - grants and status after ANRF

accepted.s: The SERB Overseas Fellowship is intended primarily for:
o: Scientists working only in agricultural universities
accepted.x: The SERB Overseas Fellowship is intended for diaspora researchers.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an overseas fellowship for diaspora researchers from domestic return fellowships.
accepted.sec: SERB - grants and status after ANRF

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the status of SERB after the ANRF Act, 2023:
1. The ANRF Act repealed the SERB Act, 2008.
2. SERB was subsumed into ANRF.
3. All schemes previously associated with SERB were discontinued.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The ANRF Act, 2023 repealed the SERB Act, 2008 and subsumed SERB into ANRF. The schemes continue under ANRF, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Spot the false extreme statement that converts institutional subsumption into complete discontinuation of schemes.
accepted.sec: SERB - grants and status after ANRF

accepted.s: Which fellowship is intended to repatriate scientists to India?
accepted.x: The Ramanujan Fellowship is a return fellowship intended to repatriate scientists to India.
accepted.tq: Match the fellowship name with its distinctive return or overseas purpose.
accepted.sec: SERB - grants and status after ANRF

accepted.s: Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship is associated with which field?
accepted.x: The Ramalingaswami Re-entry Fellowship is a return fellowship in life sciences.
accepted.tq: Use the disciplinary focus to distinguish closely related re-entry fellowships.
accepted.sec: SERB - grants and status after ANRF

accepted.s: The monthly fellowship amount mentioned for the Prime Minister’s Research Fellowship is:
accepted.x: The monthly amount mentioned for the Prime Minister’s Research Fellowship is ₹70,000–80,000.
accepted.tq: Compare the numerical ranges carefully; the correct range lies between the lower and higher distractors.
accepted.sec: SERB - grants and status after ANRF

accepted.s: Which of the following sets consists entirely of CSIR laboratories or centres located in Hyderabad?
o: NIGST, NIO Regional Centre and CCMB
accepted.x: CCMB, IICT and NGRI are CSIR laboratories or centres located in Hyderabad. CDFD and NIAB are DBT institutions, while INCOIS and NIGST are non-CSIR institutions.
accepted.tq: Classify each institution by both location and parent organisation before selecting the all-correct set.
accepted.sec: CSIR and DBT laboratories in AP and Telangana

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: CDFD is a DBT institution in Hyderabad. NGRI is a CSIR laboratory, NIAB is associated with DBT, and INCOIS is non-CSIR.
accepted.tq: Verify the parent organisation first, since the location alone is common to several institutions.
accepted.sec: CSIR and DBT laboratories in AP and Telangana

accepted.s: Which one of the following is a non-CSIR institution located in Hyderabad?
accepted.x: INCOIS is a non-CSIR institution located in Hyderabad. CCMB, IICT and NGRI are CSIR institutions there.
accepted.tq: Find the odd institutional category while keeping the common location constant.
accepted.sec: CSIR and DBT laboratories in AP and Telangana

accepted.s: The NIO Regional Centre mentioned in relation to Andhra Pradesh is located at:
accepted.x: The NIO Regional Centre in Andhra Pradesh is located at Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Use location-based recall and distinguish the regional centre from Hyderabad institutions.
accepted.sec: CSIR and DBT laboratories in AP and Telangana

accepted.s: The 2026 MoU between Bullayya College, Visakhapatnam, and IICT focuses on converting shrimp waste into:
accepted.x: The MoU focuses on converting shrimp waste into chitin and glucosamine.
accepted.tq: Link the local resource to the specific value-added products rather than to a generic biotechnology output.
accepted.sec: CSIR and DBT laboratories in AP and Telangana

accepted.s: NEERI-ZAR was mentioned in connection with which situation?
accepted.x: NEERI-ZAR was mentioned in relation to the Assam floods.
accepted.tq: Match the technology or institutional initiative with the specific current environmental event.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: CSIO was mentioned in relation to which activity?
accepted.x: CSIO was mentioned in the context of technology transfers.
accepted.tq: Identify the activity associated with the institution instead of inferring a broader administrative role.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The consolidation of DBT institutes is associated with which organisation?
accepted.x: BRIC is associated with the consolidation of DBT institutes.
accepted.tq: Match the organisational acronym with the structural reform it represents.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following has been proposed in debates concerning the governance and evaluation of science institutions?
o: Evaluating laboratories only on the basis of student enrolment
Restricting all laboratory appointments to overseas scientists
Reserving half of the top DST, DBT and CSIR posts for mid-career scientists and judging laboratories by patents and technology transfer
accepted.x: The proposals included reserving half of the top posts for mid-career scientists and evaluating laboratories through patents and technology transfer.
accepted.tq: Select the precise paired proposal; the distractors replace the stated reform with absolute institutional changes.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which of the following represents an Andhra Pradesh-specific science and technology application highlighted in the context of local development?
o: Shrimp-waste value chain with IICT and research at AIIMS Mangalagiri
Only the establishment of NIGST at Hyderabad
The Ramanujan Fellowship for repatriated scientists
The Assam flood response by NEERI-ZAR alone
accepted.x: The Andhra Pradesh angle includes the shrimp-waste value chain with IICT and research at AIIMS Mangalagiri.
accepted.tq: Combine the two state-specific applications and exclude institutions or initiatives belonging to other contexts.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: HANSA-3 (NG) has the distinction of being:
o: The first indigenously developed aircraft to be commercially manufactured in India
The first Indian satellite launched by a private company
The first aircraft jointly developed by India and DAE
The first Indian aircraft powered exclusively by hydrogen
accepted.x: HANSA-3 (NG) is the first indigenously developed aircraft to be commercially manufactured in India.
accepted.tq: Use the first-achievement wording carefully and distinguish aircraft manufacturing from satellite or propulsion claims.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
